ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $\triangle ABC$ is folded along $EF$ such that point $A$ falls on point ${A}^{\prime}$. $BP$ and $CP$ are respectively the angle bisectors of $\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$. If $\angle P=30^\circ$ and $\angle {A}^{\prime}EB=20^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle {A}^{\prime}FC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
since $BP$ and $CP$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$ respectively,\\
it follows that $\angle PBD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABD$ and $\angle BCP=\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA$.\\
Also, since $\angle PBD=\angle P+\angle PCB$,\\
we have $\angle P=\angle PBD−\angle PCB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABD−\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA=\frac{1}{2}(\angle ABD−\angle ACB)$,\\
and since $\angle ABD=\angle A+\angle ACB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABD−\angle ACB=\angle A$,\\
thus $\angle P=\frac{1}{2}\angle A$,\\
and hence $\angle A=2\angle P=2\times 30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
Given that: $\angle A\prime =\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle 1=\angle A\prime +\angle A\prime EB=60^\circ+20^\circ=80^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle A\prime FC=\angle A+\angle 1=60^\circ+80^\circ=\boxed{140^\circ}$,\\

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, $\triangle ABC$ is folded along $EF$ such that point $A$ falls on point ${A}^{\prime}$. $BP$ and $CP$ are respectively the angle bisectors of $\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$. If $\angle P=30^\circ$ and $\angle {A}^{\prime}EB=20^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle {A}^{\prime}FC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
since $BP$ and $CP$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$ respectively,\\
it follows that $\angle PBD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABD$ and $\angle BCP=\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA$.\\
Also, since $\angle PBD=\angle P+\angle PCB$,\\
we have $\angle P=\angle PBD−\angle PCB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABD−\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA=\frac{1}{2}(\angle ABD−\angle ACB)$,\\
and since $\angle ABD=\angle A+\angle ACB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABD−\angle ACB=\angle A$,\\
thus $\angle P=\frac{1}{2}\angle A$,\\
and hence $\angle A=2\angle P=2\times 30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
Given that: $\angle A\prime =\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle 1=\angle A\prime +\angle A\prime EB=60^\circ+20^\circ=80^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle A\prime FC=\angle A+\angle 1=60^\circ+80^\circ=\boxed{140^\circ}$,\\
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the diagram, D, B, and C lie on the same horizontal line, with D to the left of B and C to the right. Point A is above B, E lies on segment AB, and F lies on segment AC. The fold line is EF, and after folding, A maps to A′, which is shown to the left of E and connected to E and F. Lines BP and CP meet at P on the left side of the figure. The given angle near E is ∠A′EB = 20°, and ∠P = 30°.

Reasoning: Since BP bisects ∠ABD, ∠PBD = 1/2∠ABD. Since CP bisects ∠ACD, and C, B, D are collinear, this gives ∠BCP = 1/2∠ACB. From the diagram, ∠P is the difference between these two half-angles, so ∠P = 1/2(∠ABD − ∠ACB). Because ∠ABD is the exterior angle of triangle ABC, ∠ABD = ∠A + ∠ACB. Therefore ∠P = 1/2∠A. Given ∠P = 30°, we get ∠A = 60°.

Folding preserves angles, so ∠EA′F = ∠EAF = ∠A = 60°. With ∠A′EB = 20°, the exterior angle marked in the folded triangle is 60° + 20° = 80°. Finally, ∠A′FC is the sum of this 80° angle and the original apex angle 60°, so ∠A′FC = 80° + 60° = 140°.
